scope: Scoped pass after the separate-science split: exam-structure claims, required-practical numbers, tier wrappers, course-scope sentences, board naming. Facts were checked earlier today.

findings.claim: The Higher Tier wrapper opened before 'Strong and Weak Acids' also enclosed the 'How a Titration Works' collapsible.
findings.truth: Strong and weak acids is Higher Tier only, but describing how to carry out a titration is core content in this course. The wrapper must close before the titration block.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.2.6 (HT only) vs 4.4.2.5 Titrations - only the calculation bullet is marked (HT Only)

findings.claim: A titration ... 'It is not one of the required practicals for this course.'
findings.truth: A titration is a required practical on this course (second in the chemistry list): determination of the reacting volumes of a strong acid and a strong alkali by titration.

findings.claim: A Higher Tier wrapper opened at the top of the lesson, flagging percentage yield and atom economy as Higher Tier.
findings.truth: Calculating percentage yield from an actual yield, and calculating atom economy from a balanced equation, are core. Only 'calculate the theoretical mass of a product from a given mass of reactant' and 'explain why a particular reaction pathway is chosen' are Higher Tier, and neither is taught here.

findings.claim: Molar concentration (mol/dm3) and molar gas volumes sat outside the Higher Tier wrapper, so Foundation students were shown them as core.
findings.truth: Both are Higher Tier only in this course. The wrapper now opens at 'Molar Concentrations' and closes after the gas volume worked examples.

findings.claim: Two Higher Tier opening tags at the top of the lesson, with one closing tag, left the whole lesson - titration method, chemical cells, batteries and fuel cells - inside a Higher Tier wrapper.
findings.truth: All of that is core content. The wrapper was being used to mean 'separate science only'.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.2.5 (describe how to carry out titrations), 4.5.2.1 Cells and batteries, 4.5.2.2 Fuel cells - none marked HT only

findings.claim: The 'Titration Calculations' section (M1V1 = M2V2, concentrations in mol/dm3) carried no tier wrapper of its own.
findings.truth: Calculating chemical quantities in titrations with concentrations in mol/dm3 and g/dm3 is Higher Tier only, so this section is now wrapped.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.2.5 (HT Only) bullet; Required practical 2 (HT only) concentration determination

findings.claim: The hydrogen fuel cell half equations were labelled 'Higher tier:' in prose only; after the stray wrapper was removed they would have read as core.
findings.truth: Writing the half equations for the electrode reactions in a hydrogen fuel cell is Higher Tier only, so the paragraph is now inside a wrapper.

findings.claim: Description is 103 characters: 'How bonding affects properties, states of matter, and the structures of diamond, graphite and graphene.'
findings.truth: The house limit is 100 characters. Pre-existing and outside this pass, so not edited.
findings.evidence: validator limit in the checker brief

findings.claim: Required practicals are named but never numbered anywhere in the unit (lessons 7, 8, 9, 12).
findings.truth: Each named practical exists in the chemistry list with the right method: soluble salt from an insoluble base (1), titration (2), electrolysis of aqueous solutions with inert electrodes (3), temperature changes in reacting solutions (4). No number needed changing because no number is stated.

summary: No exam-structure claim survives anywhere in this unit (no paper count, duration, mark total, 'Combined Science' or 'Trilogy' text), so nothing needed rewriting for the two-paper Chemistry structure. Seven tier and scope faults were fixed: the titration 'not a required practical' sentence, the titration method wrongly flagged Higher Tier in lesson 7, the inverted wrappers in lessons 11 and 12, and two genuinely Higher Tier passages (titration calculations, fuel cell half equations) that had no wrapper. Existing Higher Tier wrappers in lessons 5, 6, 8 and 9 were checked against the chemistry spec and are correct as they stand.
